title: Prefetch heuristics and quantization validation pilot for token-economy improvements
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Executive summary:
This initiative runs a tightly scoped pilot to validate two orthogonal cost levers on request traffic patterns: (1) lightweight prefetching/prefix-KV heuristics to increase effective batching and cache hit-rate for common prompt families, and (2) a controlled quantization validation matrix (INT8/FP16 mixed profiles) to measure output fidelity vs unit-cost on production-like workloads. Goal: identify 10-20% per-token cost savings for interactive generative endpoints without regressions in quality or latency SLOs, and produce deterministic roll-forward criteria for wider rollout.

Scope and success criteria:
- Traffic slice: 5 medium-volume customers across chat and completion routes (70M tokens/day combined).
- Metrics: token-cost reduction, 95th/99th latency impact, quality regression (ROUGE/embedding similarity + human sample review), cache hit rate delta, rollout safety score.
- Success threshold: >=10% cost reduction at equal-or-better 95p latency and <=1.5% measurable quality regression on eval prompts.

Work done so far (progress updates):
- 2026-02-12: Kickoff - product, runtime eng, and SRE aligned on guardrails and observability events; initial customer cohort selected (see links).
- 2026-02-20: Engineering delivered prefetching prototype that identifies stable prefix clusters and emits eager KV warms for repeated provenance tokens; CPU cost baseline measured on staging. (ENG-33991)
- 2026-02-28: Quantization experiment harness completed; model variants generated for two quant profiles and integrated into canary routing. Quick smoke tests run for hallucination-prone prompts. (ENG-33992)
- 2026-03-04: Observability: added per-request delta metrics in Console: cache-hit, warmed-kv, quant-profile, latency tokens; dashboard draft created for pilot.
- 2026-03-09: Initial A/B run (24h) on 10% of cohort traffic: mean token-cost -8.7%, cache-hit +14pp, 95p latency +6ms; automated QA flagged 0.9% divergence on structured-output tests. Human review queued.

Trade-offs and open decisions:
- Prefetch aggressiveness vs latency: more aggressive warming reduces token cost but may add head latency if miss-rate increases; decided to prefer conservative warming (thresholds: cluster stability >= 0.6, expected reuse >= 3 requests).
- Quant profile rollout granularity: per-route vs global. Early tests favor route-level control to isolate regressions for chat flows.
- Monitoring signal surface: need to expand hallucination-specific checks (entity hallucination detection). Action: Eng to add a synthetic prompt set running continuously.

Review feedback and approvals:
- 2026-03-06 PM review (Asha Patel): asked for clearer rollback triggers and customer opt-in controls; SRE provided SLO-based fallback (auto-disable on 95p latency +10% spike).
- 2026-03-10 Design review (Nina Park): requested telemetry to be surfaced in Console rollout page and a short customer-facing explainer. Design is drafting copy.

Artifacts and links:
- Pilot PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821
- Prototype design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/53921/Prefetch+Heuristics+Pilot
- Observability dashboard (Console): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/prefetch-quant-pilot
- Human review sheet (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-prefetch-quant-human-review

Next steps (short horizon 2 weeks):
- 2026-03-13 to 2026-03-18: extend A/B to 40% of cohort, run full quantization matrix (INT8, mixed FP16/INT8) and collect metric matrix.
- 2026-03-19: product + eng + SRE sync to evaluate go/no-go; if pass, prepare rollout playbook and customer opt-in UI.
- 2026-03-22: ship customer-facing explainer and enable opt-in toggle for pilot participants.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: silent quality regressions on niche prompts. Mitigation: expand synthetic prompt bank and require manual signoff for any quant profile that fails a threshold.
- Risk: increased tail latency for cold prefixes. Mitigation: adaptive backoff in prefetcher and immediate fallback to non-prefetched path on spike.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Capture per-customer savings and annotate in cost dashboards to build business case for Dedicated/reserved capacity optimization features.
- If successful, translate prefetch heuristics into a runtime-config profile and add to Optimize recommendations as a suggested optimization with estimated ROI.
